title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 67
paragraphs: These, I say, were thus directing their march. Meanwhile, while the other Greeks on the king's side were deliberately slack in the fight, the Boeotians fought with the Athenians for a long time. The Thebans who took the Median side had no small zeal for the cause, and they fought and were not slack — so that three hundred of them, the first and best of all, fell there by the hands of the Athenians. When these too turned to flight, they fled to Thebes, not to the same place as the Persians; and the main body of the other allies fled without having fought steadily with anyone or shown any deeds of valor.
